correctness.rationale: Every independent set in the crown graph is either contained in one bipartition class or is a single deleted-matching pair \(\{a_i,b_i\}\). In a proper coloring satisfying the requirement of at least two color-dominating vertices in every color class, a pure class and a paired class cannot coexist: one endpoint of the paired class sees no vertex of the pure class, leaving at most one color-dominating vertex in that pair. If there are no paired classes, there can be at most one pure class on each side, forcing the two-color bipartition coloring. If any paired class occurs, all classes are paired, so covering all vertices forces the \(n\) deleted-matching pairs. Both constructions meet the two-color-dominating-vertex condition, so the spectrum is exactly \(\{2,n\}\), with the two realizing partitions unique up to color-name permutation. The package's exhaustive set-partition check for \(3\le n\le5\) corroborates the structural proof but is not used to infer the universal theorem.
residual_risks: The result is for the constant sequence \(S=(2,2,\ldots)\) and crown graphs only.
